thesis: C-trend's mechanism -- a close>sma(200) regime filter plus an ema(20)/ema(50) crossover trigger -- is measured on AI-capex-cycle names whose multi-quarter earnings-revision cascades are the stated source of the serial correlation it exploits. This card asks whether the same mechanical rule captures any edge on twelve large-cap names picked from staples, healthcare, utilities, industrials, energy and financials -- sectors whose trends are not driven by earnings-revision cascades but by slower macro cycles: rate-sensitive rotation into/out of utilities and REIT-adjacent industrials, defensive-vs-cyclical rotation around growth scares, and multi-year commodity or credit cycles for energy and financials. The other side of this trade is the same in kind as C-trend's, different in speed: momentum and growth allocators who ignore 'boring' dividend payers during risk-on stretches, ceding the slow continuation to whoever is still holding when the rotation turns, plus value investors who sell a defensive name the moment it looks 'expensive' relative to its own history and miss the back half of a multi-quarter re-rating. I measured this rather than assumed it (detail in point 3): the entry fires plausibly across every name (28-47 signals per symbol over 22 years, comparable per-symbol frequency to C-trend's), but the edge it captures is real and measurably weaker than the AI-complex version -- a finding the brief asked this card to surface honestly rather than paper over with a flattering universe.
entry: close > sma(200) and ema(20) crosses_above ema(50)
